study type: Cohort study (non-inferiority design, using retrospective and prospective data)
exposure: Mode of birth (in water vs. out of water) among women using intrapartum water immersion
outcome: Neonatal unit admission with respiratory support (neonatal composite)
Administration of antibiotics within 48 hours of birth (neonatal composite)
cohort: The study included 73,229 women without antenatal or intrapartum risk factors who used intrapartum water immersion, excluding those who received obstetric or anaesthetic interventions before birth.
finding: Among women using water immersion during labour, remaining in the pool and giving birth in water was not associated with an increase in the incidence of adverse primary maternal or neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Rates of obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) and adverse neonatal composite outcomes were no higher among waterbirths compared with births out of water among women using intrapartum water immersion.
followup_time: 48 hours after birth (for neonatal composite outcomes)
